newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end with solid gains, tracking Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end with solid gains, tracking Dow rally.

text.p: ** UK shares end with solid gains, tracking a steep
rally on Wall Street after news of a smaller-than-
expected 0.1 percent rise in U.S. CPI. Bonds, gilts
surge on inflation data.
** British Airways jumps as SBC Warburg repeats "buy."
"The markets had factored in a lot of bad news and now it's running on relief," said one dealer.
Yet many market watchers questioned how long the relief rally would last.
"These (CPI) figures clearly show that inflation remains subdued, but it won't stop the Fed from tightening," said DKB International economist Nick Stamenkovic.
He said the next obstacles for the market are the U.S. employment cost index and gross domestic product data, due at the end of the month.
"I can't see today's rally being sustained for too long," he added.
Just last week, a larger-than-expected rise in the U.S. producer price index raised fears the Federal Reserve would tighten more aggressively to stamp out inflation.
Stock strategist David Aserkoff of Credit Suisse First Boston said he didn't expect the increase at the producer level to translate into higher consumer prices in upcoming months.
"Higher producer prices won't filter down anytime soon. It was a bit of a market concern, but it's not an economic reality," he said.
Yet Aserkoff said he was still looking for the Fed to tighten further at its next policy meeting next month.
"This is a bit of a holiday in the sun for the markets, but I don't think this is a sign that the Fed is not going to tighten further," Aserkoff said.
Dealers also noted that UK rates are set to move higher after the May 1 election.
They were waiting for UK data on unemployment and public sector borrowing, due for release on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, worries about the possibility of a hung Parliament is likely to continue to unnerve investors over the near-term, dealers said.
"The biggest single factor at the moment is still Wall Street and everyone knows you can't trust Wall Street," said another dealer.

Among individual stocks, shares in Zeneca Plc, the worst performer in the FTSE 100, tumbled 37p, or two percent, to 1797p, after Swiss rival Roche Holding AG, frequently named as a possible bidder, made no mention of any bid intentions when reporting first-quarter sales results.
Among the best performers on the FTSE 100 were shares in Great Universal Stores Plc, which added 18p, or 2.8 percent, to 651-1/2.
The shares jumped on an upbeat press report, adding to Monday's rise on the back of its acquisition of Direct Marketing Technology and an upgrade from SBC Warburg.
The Times said the retailing group's most recent acquisition was a good match for Experian, which GUS acquired last year.

Shares in British Airways Plc firmed 7p to 516-1/2p, after SBC Warburg repeated a "buy" rating and a 750p price target in a review of the transport sector, dealers said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
